title: Payment API deployment runbook
text:
Payment API deployment runbook
For release 2.8 and later, deploy the payment-api service using the blue-green strategy. Confirm readiness probes pass for all pods before shifting traffic. The service listens on port 8080. The readiness endpoint is /health/ready. If readiness fails after deployment, stop traffic shifting and inspect application logs and dependency health.

title: Payment API legacy deployment notes
text:
Legacy payment-api deployment notes
Older releases used a rolling deployment and listened on port 8000. This document applies only to releases before 2.8 and is retained for historical reference. Do not use these instructions for current releases.

title: Payment API timeout configuration
text:
Payment API timeout configuration
The outbound payment-provider connection timeout is 10 seconds and the response timeout is 25 seconds. These values are configured with PAYMENT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and PAYMENT_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. The previous 30-second connect timeout was removed in release 2.7.

title: Legacy timeout configuration
text:
Legacy timeout configuration
The payment service used a 30-second connection timeout. This setting is obsolete from release 2.7 onward. Current deployments should use the configuration reference for the active release.

title: Payment API 503 troubleshooting
text:
Payment API 503 troubleshooting
A sudden increase in HTTP 503 responses can occur when all application instances fail readiness checks, when the database connection pool is exhausted, or when the upstream payment provider is unavailable. Check readiness status, pool utilization, and provider health before assigning a root cause. A 503 alone does not prove which dependency failed.

title: Database connection pool guidance
text:
Database connection pool guidance
The payment-api production pool defaults to 40 maximum connections per instance. Pool exhaustion is indicated by active connections reaching the configured maximum together with connection acquisition timeout messages. Do not increase the pool without checking the database server connection limit and the number of application instances.

title: Database pool incident 2026-09-14
text:
Incident: payment-api elevated 503 responses on 2026-09-14
Impact: 18 minutes of elevated payment failures. Root cause: a connection leak introduced in build pay-2.8.4 prevented connections from returning to the pool. Evidence: active connections reached 40 per instance; logs showed 'connection acquisition timeout'; database CPU remained below 55%. Mitigation: rollback to pay-2.8.3. Follow-up: fix connection lifecycle and add pool saturation alert.

title: Deployment incident 2026-10-02
text:
Incident: payment-api 503 errors after deployment on 2026-10-02
Impact: 11 minutes of partial payment failures. Root cause: readiness probe path was changed to /readyz in a release, but the service still exposed /health/ready. New pods never became ready and the load balancer returned 503. Evidence: application process was healthy; readiness probe returned 404; no database pool saturation. Mitigation: restore /health/ready and redeploy.

title: Payment provider status investigation
text:
Payment provider dependency investigation
When provider failures are suspected, inspect provider status events and outbound request error rates. Provider unavailability commonly produces elevated connect errors or 5xx responses from the provider. Correlate timestamps with application errors. Do not infer provider failure solely from customer-facing 503 responses.

title: Release 2.8.4 change summary
text:
Release 2.8.4 change summary
Release 2.8.4 refactored payment-provider response handling and database transaction cleanup. The release was deployed to production on 2026-09-14 at 09:05 UTC. The database cleanup change modified connection release behavior. Monitor connection pool utilization after rollout.

title: Release 2.8.5 change summary
text:
Release 2.8.5 change summary
Release 2.8.5 was deployed on 2026-10-02 at 14:20 UTC. It included a readiness probe configuration update intended to standardize health checks. The configured probe path in the deployment manifest was /readyz.

title: Kubernetes readiness probes
text:
Kubernetes readiness probes
A readiness probe determines whether a container is ready to receive traffic. A failed readiness probe removes the pod from service endpoints but does not necessarily restart the container. Check the configured path, port, response code, and application health endpoint. A 404 commonly indicates a path mismatch.

title: Load balancer 503 behavior
text:
Load balancer 503 behavior
The internal load balancer can return HTTP 503 when no healthy backend endpoints are available. Check endpoint membership and pod readiness before investigating application-level request handling. This behavior is independent of whether the application process is running.

title: Payment API observability dashboard guide
text:
Payment API observability guide
For payment-api incidents, inspect request rate, 5xx rate, pod readiness, restart count, database pool active connections, connection acquisition latency, and upstream provider errors. Compare each metric against the deployment timestamp. Preserve UTC timestamps when correlating logs and events.

title: Service endpoint reference
text:
Payment API endpoint reference
The current payment-api exposes GET /health/live and GET /health/ready on port 8080. /health/live indicates process liveness. /health/ready indicates readiness to receive traffic. There is no /readyz endpoint in release 2.8.5.

title: Database server capacity policy
text:
Database server capacity policy
The production database supports a maximum of 500 client connections. Capacity planning must account for maximum pool size multiplied by the maximum number of application instances, plus reserved connections for administration and background jobs. Any pool-size change requires capacity review.

title: Incident INC-2417: provider outage
text:
Incident INC-2417: payment provider outage
A provider-side regional outage caused elevated payment-provider 502 responses for 23 minutes. Application database pool utilization stayed below 50%. Provider status events began at 16:02 UTC and recovered at 16:25 UTC. Mitigation was routing eligible traffic to the secondary provider.

title: Incident INC-2391: database saturation
text:
Incident INC-2391: database connection saturation
A batch job opened more database connections than expected, exhausting the shared database connection budget. Payment-api logs showed acquisition timeouts and pool utilization at maximum. Database server connections reached 492 of 500. Mitigation was pausing the batch job and reducing its concurrency.

title: Authentication service troubleshooting
text:
Authentication service troubleshooting
For JWT validation failures, inspect token issuer, audience, signing key identifier, expiration, and clock skew. HTTP 401 generally indicates authentication failure; HTTP 403 generally indicates an authenticated caller lacks permission. Do not rotate signing keys until validating the key identifier and issuer configuration.

title: API gateway rate limiting
text:
API gateway rate limiting
The gateway returns HTTP 429 when a client exceeds its configured request quota. Inspect rate-limit headers and gateway metrics. A 429 response is distinct from a backend-generated 503 response.

title: Service ownership and escalation
text:
Service ownership and escalation
The payment-api team owns application code, health endpoints, and database pool configuration. The platform team owns Kubernetes deployment manifests and internal load balancer configuration. The database team owns server connection capacity. During incidents, collect evidence before assigning ownership.

title: Post-deployment verification checklist
text:
Post-deployment verification checklist
After deploying payment-api: verify desired and ready pod counts match; call /health/ready; confirm load balancer backend endpoints are healthy; inspect 5xx rate; verify database pool utilization; inspect upstream provider errors. Record deployment version and UTC timestamp. Roll back if service health does not recover within the release's approved rollback window.

title: Payment API cache behavior
text:
Payment API cache behavior
The payment-api uses a short-lived in-memory cache for merchant configuration. Cache misses can increase database reads but do not directly cause HTTP 503 responses. Investigate pool saturation only when supported by connection metrics and logs.

title: Incident response evidence standards
text:
Incident response evidence standards
A root-cause statement must be supported by at least one direct signal and a corroborating source where available. Separate observed facts from hypotheses. Include document IDs, timestamps, and confidence. If evidence conflicts or is incomplete, state the uncertainty and list the next diagnostic action. Never present a hypothesis as a confirmed root cause.

title: Payment API deployment note for release 2.8.6
text:
Release 2.8.6 change summary
Release 2.8.6 restores the readiness probe path to /health/ready and adds a deployment validation that compares manifest probe paths with the service endpoint reference. This release does not change database pool sizing or provider timeout values.

title: Unrelated frontend build troubleshooting
text:
Frontend build troubleshooting
If a browser bundle fails to compile, clear the package manager cache, reinstall dependencies, and inspect TypeScript compiler output. This document concerns the web frontend and does not describe payment-api runtime or infrastructure behavior.
